title: Edge-tiered trace routing proxy for hot/cold Tempo backends
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an edge-side routing proxy that intelligently routes spans to hot (fast, short-retention) and cold (compressed, long-retention) Tempo storage tiers. The proxy will accept OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP, perform lightweight schema validation and tenant retention lookups, and attach a retention hint header for downstream ingestion. For queries that request cold data, the proxy will provide an on-demand rehydration path that triggers a background copy from cold archive into the hot tier (or a query-time read-through) and surface an ETA to the caller. Goals: reduce hot-storage costs by moving cold spans to cheaper tiering, maintain query UX for recent and on-demand historical reads, and preserve per-tenant retention/PII redaction policies.
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created by Ava. Initial proposal drafted after ops spike in SRE weekly. Motivation: hot storage costs spiking on low-value long-tail spans.

2025-02-14: Design sync with storage team (Liam O'Neill). Decided to add a simple retention-hint header rather than mutate incoming payloads. Agreed to use existing tenant retention table in config-service.

2025-02-17: Prototype completed for OTLP/gRPC ingress that tags spans with X-Redwood-Retention-Hint and routes to two Kafka topics (hot/cold) depending on retention policy. Latency added: ~1.8ms median at 95th percentile under load test (10k/s).
2025-02-20: Privacy review notes: cold tier must apply PII redaction pipeline before archival. Security requires KMS encryption-at-rest for cold archives. Jun to schedule security review.

2025-02-26: Implemented query-time rehydration API (v0) and added a rehydration job definition to batch-worker. Integration tests passing in staging with synthetic traces. Planning canary rollout to a single tenant with <1% traffic next week.
notes: Trade-offs: upfront routing increases write-path complexity but is cheaper than retroactive reprocessing. We accept slightly higher ingress latency to avoid large batch migrations.
Rollout plan: feature flag for retention-hint header, start with synthetic spans -> internal teams -> low-volume customers -> broader rollout with telemetry-driven gating.

Monitoring: dashboards for write latency, rehydration queue length, successful rehydrations, and cold-tier read latency. Alert when rehydration backlog > 5k jobs or median hot-write latency increases > 15%.
Open questions: quota accounting for rehydration reads, UX for clients waiting on historical query rehydration, and pricing model for charged rehydrates.
